text:
Alice Wang: heads up — proposing a phased unpin of runtime v2.14.2 for quantized llama3x variants only to mitigate KV-cache cost and p95 regressions we saw overnight.

Raj Patel: why target just quant models? is this a behavioral change in the kernel?

Alice Wang: not a correctness issue — it's an execution path cost increase. KV cache misses + slightly different kernel scheduling for quant path spiked CPU/GPU usage; longseq workloads saw token cost ~2.7x for a short window.

Maria Gomez: any customer-facing errors?

Kevin Lee: CS reported one longform timeout from a beta tenant, but no broad escalations.

Alice Wang: proposed plan: do an isolated unpin (runtime -> allow newer runtime) only for llama3x-quant on eu-central canary for 3h. Keep default routing pinned for longseq models. If stable, widen region and model groups.

Raj Patel: what's the exact rollback/runforward playbook if things degrade?

Alice Wang: rollback steps if thresholds hit: 
- abort canary traffic via routing -> deploybot abort
- re-pin runtime across production via deploybot
- run the smoke and perf suites and open a rollback incident
Command reference we'll use:

```
# deploybot CLI
deploybot unpin runtime 2.14.2 --models=llama3x-quant --window=3h --region=eu-central
# rollback
deploybot pin runtime 2.14.2 --scope=production
```

Maria Gomez: note — SDK needs a small shim for model config parsing (SDK v1.4.1). Staging validated. Without it some model metadata (layerwise quant flags) mis-parse and cause suboptimal kernel selection.

Kevin Lee: are older SDK clients (v1.3.x) impacted? we can't force all customers to upgrade quickly.

Raj Patel: shim is opt-in feature-detect; it falls back on legacy parsing for <v1.4.0. Should be safe, but we'll gate rollout with a feature flag.

Alice Wang: action items: 
- Alice: initiate canary unpin for llama3x-quant in eu-central (now)
- Maria: promote SDK shim to staging and add feature flag (30m)
- Raj: monitor p95 latency, error rate, KV cache hit rate, and costs; threshold for revert = p95 > baseline+5% OR errors > baseline+10%
- Kevin: draft KB/CS blurb and post in #support (done)

deploybot: notice — scheduled unpin initiated by @Alice Wang at 1712349000. Command executed:
```
deploybot unpin runtime 2.14.2 --models=llama3x-quant --window=3h --region=eu-central
```

sre-bot: Alert — 3 x 502s seen during the first 10 minutes of canary; p95 token latency ~1200ms (baseline ~320ms). Events traced to cache warming and one backend retry loop.

Raj Patel: data check — after initial spikes, p95 is trending down. If it stabilizes within next 30m we keep canary. If another spike set, we revert.

Maria Gomez: telemetry shows token latency back to baseline after ~20m for the sampled sessions. Cache hit rate improved from 54% -> 88% as the KV warmed.

Kevin Lee: support note posted: "Temporary unpin for quantized llama3x to address cost/latency anomalies; no data exposure. Internal KB: https://redwood.internal/kb/unpin-1712345678"

Alice Wang: timeline — canary end/decision at 1712352878. Revert criteria reiterated: p95 > baseline+5% OR error rate > baseline+10% over a 5m window. If revert needed, Raj will trigger pin and open a rollback incident with severity P2.

Raj Patel: I'll be on watch for those windows and will escalate immediately if thresholds crossed.

Kevin Lee: one more ask: add a short note to the release notes saying this was a targeted unpin for quant models due to runtime kernel scheduling differences, and that we're rolling out an SDK shim.

Alice Wang: agreed. We'll follow up with a short postmortem if we end up reverting. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
